subject.title: [Feature]: Script to restore session history archived by new daily-reset mechanism (introduced v2026.2+)

question: Should OpenClaw resolve reset-archive recovery through the bounded `includeFamily` read path alone, add a separate doctor-style restore/re-index recovery command, or reject mutation-style restore in favor of documented read-only access?
rationale: Current main only has active-missing fallback, while the remaining choices change model-facing history access, archived transcript exposure, and possibly persisted session metadata, so maintainer intent is needed before implementing or closing the broader recovery request.

options.title: Land Bounded Family History
options.body: Use the open `includeFamily` PR as the canonical first fix and leave mutation-style restore for a later explicit recovery decision.

options.title: Add Doctor Recovery
options.body: Sponsor a separate `openclaw doctor --fix` or recovery command that restores/re-indexes archives with metadata, backups, retention checks, and tests.

options.title: Reject Restore Mutation
options.body: Keep archives read-only, document the supported retrieval/export path, and close restore/re-index script requests once read-only access has shipped.

recommendation.title: Land Bounded Family History
recommendation.body: Use the open `includeFamily` PR as the canonical first fix and leave mutation-style restore for a later explicit recovery decision.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent commit and release history ties this person to the landed reset-archive fallback and current release behavior.
